title: Haitian Creole Foundations
subtitle: From first Kreyòl sounds to your first everyday conversation.
description: An A0-to-A1 Haitian Creole course that develops listening, speaking, reading, sentence building, and writing together from the first module.

courseOverview.recommendedSequence: Complete the eight modules in order. Each module reuses earlier language while adding one practical communication layer.
courseOverview.summary: Start with sound and spelling, then progress through greetings, identity, objects, actions, questions, numbers, time, and a first cumulative conversation.

moduleSummary.title: Sounds of Kreyòl
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Give true beginners enough sound and spelling confidence to approach their first spoken and written Kreyòl without treating English spelling as a guide.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Use Sounds in a Mini Exchange

moduleSummary.title: Bonjou!
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Move from isolated sounds into the first complete social interactions a learner can understand and use immediately.

moduleSummary.title: Who Are You?
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Give learners a practical identity exchange they can understand and produce with increasing independence.

moduleSummary.title: Talking About Things
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Expand from people to concrete objects so learners can understand and produce useful noun-centered sentences.

moduleSummary.title: What Are You Doing?
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Introduce the learner to useful action language without overloading the course with abstract grammar terminology.

moduleSummary.title: Questions & Answers
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Turn memorized statements into flexible two-way communication by practicing common question-and-answer structures.

moduleSummary.title: Numbers, Time & Everyday Life
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Give learners practical language for quantities, basic time, and routine information they are likely to encounter early.

moduleSummary.title: My First Kreyòl Conversation
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Consolidate A0-to-A1 foundations into a small but meaningful conversation the learner can understand and produce.

authoringGuidance: This course must use subjectSlug haitian-creole, courseSlug haitian-creole-foundations, catalogSlug haitian-creole, and profileId language.
English is the current source/instruction locale; the language being learned is Kreyòl Ayisyen.
Use official Kreyòl orthography and preserve meaningful diacritics and apostrophes.
Every module follows an integrated Learn → Listen → Speak → Read → Build → Write → Use it → Review rhythm across its topic sequence.
voice_input is transcript-based speaking practice. Do not claim phoneme-level pronunciation scoring.
Use locale ht-HT for authored speech/listening activities unless a specific provider requires the ht fallback.
Do not use code_input or pseudocode_input anywhere in this course.
Do not assume terminal, code-editor, filesystem, or programming workspace behavior.
Module 1 is intentionally free; modules 2-8 inherit the paid course access policy.

Treat module, section, topic, sketch, and activity counts as content-driven rather than quota-driven. Preserve the eight course learning stages, but use only the structure needed to teach each stage clearly and naturally.

assessmentAndDelivery.suggestedBeginnerRhythm: Complete one or two topics per study session and speak aloud during every listening/speaking topic.
toolingSuggestions: Audio playback with Kreyòl speech locale support
Speech transcription with ht/ht-HT support when available
Text and word-bank practice in the learner workspace

modules.title: Sounds of Kreyòl
modules.description: Build a first sound-to-spelling map for Kreyòl and begin recognizing, saying, reading, arranging, and writing short high-frequency words.
modules.purpose: Give true beginners enough sound and spelling confidence to approach their first spoken and written Kreyòl without treating English spelling as a guide.
learningObjectives: Recognize core Kreyòl sound and spelling patterns in short familiar words.
Listen for and repeat short sound patterns and first words.
Read, arrange, and write a small set of high-frequency words using official Kreyòl spelling.
guidedExercises: Learn or notice the target language in a short, beginner-safe context.
Listen and speak using transcript-based speaking practice where appropriate.
Read, arrange, write, use the language in context, then review it cumulatively.

sections.title: Learn, Listen & Speak
sections.description: Introduce the module language, hear it in context, and begin producing it aloud.

topics.title: Notice Kreyòl Sounds
topics.summary: Learn the first sound and spelling patterns that make written Kreyòl predictable.
learningGoals: Understand the Kreyòl language target introduced in Notice Kreyòl Sounds.
Use the target through at least one receptive skill and one productive skill.
Preserve official Kreyòl spelling and meaningful diacritics when reading or writing.

topics.title: Listen and Say First Sounds
topics.summary: Connect short Kreyòl sound patterns with what you hear and say.
learningGoals: Understand the Kreyòl language target introduced in Listen and Say First Sounds.
Use the target through at least one receptive skill and one productive skill.
Preserve official Kreyòl spelling and meaningful diacritics when reading or writing.

sections.title: Read, Build, Write & Use It
sections.description: Read and reconstruct the language, write it, use it in context, and finish with review.

topics.title: Read, Build, and Write First Words
topics.summary: Read simple words, rebuild them from visible language, and write them accurately.
learningGoals: Understand the Kreyòl language target introduced in Read, Build, and Write First Words.
Use the target through at least one receptive skill and one productive skill.
Preserve official Kreyòl spelling and meaningful diacritics when reading or writing.

topics.title: Use Sounds in a Mini Exchange
topics.summary: Use the module's sound and spelling patterns in a tiny listening-and-speaking exchange.
learningGoals: Understand the Kreyòl language target introduced in Use Sounds in a Mini Exchange.
Use the target through at least one receptive skill and one productive skill.
Preserve official Kreyòl spelling and meaningful diacritics when reading or writing.

modules.title: Bonjou!
modules.description: Use greetings, polite expressions, and simple social responses in short everyday exchanges.
modules.purpose: Move from isolated sounds into the first complete social interactions a learner can understand and use immediately.
learningObjectives: Recognize and use common greetings, polite expressions, and leave-taking language.
Ask how someone is, answer naturally, and return the question.
Follow and participate in a short connected greeting conversation.
guidedExercises: Hear useful Kreyòl before producing it.
Use listening, speaking, arranging, reading, and writing where they directly support the communication goal.
Reuse familiar language in connected turns rather than practicing isolated lines only.
quizFocus: asking and answering how someone is

sections.title: Greetings and Conversation
sections.description: Build from useful greetings and polite expressions into a complete two-way beginner conversation.

topics.title: Greetings and Polite Basics
topics.summary: Greet someone, use essential polite expressions, and close a short interaction.
learningGoals: Recognize and use Bonjou, Bonswa, Mèsi, Tanpri, Padon, and Orevwa in context.
Use listening and speaking together with simple reading and writing practice.
Choose an appropriate greeting or polite expression for a short interaction.

topics.title: Ask, Answer, and Keep It Going
topics.summary: Ask how someone is, answer naturally, and return the question.
learningGoals: Understand Kijan ou ye? when heard inside a greeting exchange.
Answer with a short complete response such as Mwen byen, mèsi.
Use E ou menm? to return the question and keep the exchange moving.

topics.title: Your First Greeting Conversation
topics.summary: Follow a complete greeting exchange, respond to each turn, and reuse the conversation pattern.
learningGoals: Follow Jan and Mari through a connected greeting conversation.
Respond to what the other participant says instead of reciting disconnected lines.
Transfer the same conversation pattern to slightly different wording.

modules.title: Who Are You?
modules.description: Introduce yourself, ask another person's name, and exchange a few simple personal details.
modules.purpose: Give learners a practical identity exchange they can understand and produce with increasing independence.
learningObjectives: Ask and answer someone's name.
Ask and answer where someone lives.
Combine greetings, names, and residence in a connected beginner conversation.
guidedExercises: Hear each new question and answer before producing it.
Integrate listening, speaking, arranging, reading, and writing around the communication goal.
Reuse Module 2 greeting language while adding name and residence information.
quizFocus: asking and answering where someone lives
returning a question with E ou menm?

sections.title: Names, Places & Introductions
sections.description: Move from exchanging names to exchanging where you live, then connect both with Module 2 greetings.

topics.title: Names and Introductions
topics.summary: Ask someone's name, say your own name, and return the question naturally.
learningGoals: Understand and use Kijan ou rele?
Answer naturally with M rele plus a name.
Use E ou menm? to return the name question.

topics.title: Where Do You Live?
topics.summary: Ask where someone lives, answer with a place, and return the question.
learningGoals: Understand and use Ki kote ou rete?
Answer with Mwen rete plus a place.
Connect a residence answer to the familiar E ou menm? follow-up.

topics.title: Meet Someone: A Full Introduction
topics.summary: Combine greetings, names, and residence into one connected first-meeting conversation.
learningGoals: Follow Jan and Mari through a complete beginner introduction.
Choose a natural next turn based on what the other person just said.
Reuse the introduction pattern with slightly different wording.

modules.title: Talking About Things
modules.description: Name everyday objects and use simple patterns to identify, describe, and point out things around you.
modules.purpose: Expand from people to concrete objects so learners can understand and produce useful noun-centered sentences.
learningObjectives: Use yon, familiar definite noun phrases, and plural yo with everyday things.
Express possession with thing + possessor and with se pou.
Use sa a and sa yo to point out things and combine them with ownership.
guidedExercises: Hear source-backed noun phrases before producing new examples.
Integrate listening, speaking, arranging, and writing around the noun-phrase meaning.
Treat a, la, an, lan, and nan as familiar chunks here; explicit article-selection rules are deferred.

sections.title: Things, Ownership & Demonstratives
sections.description: Build useful noun phrases, say who things belong to, and point out one or several objects.

topics.title: One Thing, the Thing, More Than One
topics.summary: Use yon, familiar definite noun phrases, and plural yo with everyday objects.
learningGoals: Use yon before a familiar noun.
Recognize that the definite marker follows the noun in familiar source-backed phrases.
Use yo after a noun for familiar plural phrases.

topics.title: Whose Thing Is It?
topics.summary: Put the possessor after the thing and use se pou to say who something belongs to.
learningGoals: Put the possessor after the possessed item.
Use se pou plus a person to identify ownership.
Recognize possession in singular and plural noun phrases.

topics.title: This Thing, These Things
topics.summary: Use sa a and sa yo to point out things and combine them with ownership.
learningGoals: Use sa a after a noun for one pointed-out thing.
Use sa yo after a noun for several pointed-out things.
Combine demonstratives with se pou inside a short object exchange.

modules.title: What Are You Doing?
modules.description: Talk about simple actions happening now and understand short action-centered sentences.
modules.purpose: Introduce the learner to useful action language without overloading the course with abstract grammar terminology.
learningObjectives: Use common action words in simple present statements and routines.
Use ap to describe an action in progress and recognize common short forms.
Ask Kisa ou ap fè?, answer naturally, and distinguish now from routine.
guidedExercises: Move from familiar action words into short subject-plus-action statements.
Contrast a routine with an action happening now before introducing the action question.
Integrate listening, speaking, building, and writing inside meaningful action exchanges.

sections.title: Actions, Now & Routines
sections.description: Talk about familiar actions, distinguish routines from actions happening now, and ask what someone is doing.

topics.title: Everyday Actions and Routines
topics.summary: Use common action words in simple subject-plus-action sentences and routines.
learningGoals: Recognize and use a small set of high-frequency action words.
Build simple present statements with subject + action.
Use chak jou to make a routine explicit.

topics.title: What Is Happening Now?
topics.summary: Use ap with familiar actions, recognize common short forms, and use kounyeya.
learningGoals: Use person + ap + action for an action in progress.
Recognize common shortened subjects before ap.
Use kounyeya when the current time needs to be explicit.

topics.title: What Are You Doing?
topics.summary: Ask what someone is doing, answer with a current action, and distinguish now from routine.
learningGoals: Use Kisa ou ap fè? as a complete useful question.
Answer an action question with the current-action pattern.
Distinguish kounyeya current action from chak jou routine language.

modules.title: Questions & Answers
modules.description: Recognize and produce core beginner question patterns and short natural answers.
modules.purpose: Turn memorized statements into flexible two-way communication by practicing common question-and-answer structures.
learningObjectives: Use Èske to ask familiar yes/no questions and give complete answers.
Choose familiar information-question forms based on whether you need how, what, place, person, or quantity.
Mix yes/no and information questions inside a connected beginner conversation.
guidedExercises: Start from statements and information the learner already knows from Modules 2–5.
Choose the question form from the information need rather than memorizing isolated question lists.
Integrate listening, speaking, arranging, and writing inside short question-and-answer exchanges.

sections.title: Questions & Answers
sections.description: Ask yes/no questions, choose information questions, and keep a short conversation moving.

topics.title: Yes or No? Ask with Èske
topics.summary: Turn familiar statements into yes/no questions with Èske and answer with complete sentences.
learningGoals: Recognize Èske as the Course 1 yes/no question frame.
Turn familiar statements into Èske questions.
Give a complete affirmative answer using already-known language.

topics.title: Ask for the Information You Need
topics.summary: Choose familiar question forms for how, what, where, who, and quantity.
learningGoals: Recognize familiar Kijan and Kisa questions from earlier modules.
Use Ki kote for place and Ki moun for person.
Recognize Konbyen as a quantity question without expanding into Module 7 number study.

topics.title: Keep a Question Chain Going
topics.summary: Mix yes/no and information questions with complete answers in a natural conversation.
learningGoals: Choose a question that requests new information instead of repeating known information.
Answer familiar questions with complete beginner sentences.
Follow Jan and Mari through mixed question types while preserving conversational continuity.

modules.title: Numbers, Time & Everyday Life
modules.description: Use beginner numbers and time expressions in useful everyday contexts.
modules.purpose: Give learners practical language for quantities, basic time, and routine information they are likely to encounter early.
learningObjectives: Recognize and use numbers one through twenty inside simple everyday quantities.
Recognize full-hour and half-hour clock expressions and ask time with Akilè.
Combine everyday time expressions, routines, and familiar questions in a simple schedule conversation.
guidedExercises: Hear number and clock expressions before producing new combinations.
Use numbers with familiar nouns instead of practicing isolated arithmetic.
Reuse Module 5 routines and Module 6 questions inside practical schedule exchanges.

sections.title: Numbers, Time & Everyday Life
sections.description: Count familiar things, understand basic clock time, and use time expressions inside an everyday schedule.

topics.title: Numbers and Quantities
topics.summary: Recognize numbers one through twenty and use them with familiar everyday objects.
learningGoals: Recognize Kreyòl numbers one through ten.
Recognize numbers eleven through twenty.
Use a known number before a familiar noun to express a quantity.

topics.title: Clock Time and Akilè
topics.summary: Recognize simple full-hour and half-hour expressions and ask what time an activity happens.
learningGoals: Recognize familiar full-hour expressions.
Recognize and produce edmi half-hour expressions.
Use Akilè to ask what time an activity happens.

topics.title: Everyday Time and Schedule
topics.summary: Combine day parts, familiar time expressions, routines, and Akilè in a short conversation.
learningGoals: Use maten, aswè, jòdi a, and kounyeya as everyday time expressions.
Recognize denmen maten and reuse chak jou.
Combine a clock time or day-part expression with familiar actions and questions.

modules.title: My First Kreyòl Conversation
modules.description: Combine greetings, identity, objects, actions, questions, numbers, and time in a first sustained beginner conversation.
modules.purpose: Consolidate A0-to-A1 foundations into a small but meaningful conversation the learner can understand and produce.
learningObjectives: Recognize how familiar Course 1 conversation moves connect instead of memorizing one fixed script.
Rehearse short scenes about identity, things, actions, questions, quantities, and time.
Understand and produce a sustained beginner conversation using language accumulated across the course.
guidedExercises: Map familiar conversation functions before attempting the sustained capstone.
Rehearse short scenes with listening, speaking, arranging, and writing embedded in the communication goal.
Finish with a Jan-and-Mari conversation and a second variation so success does not depend on one memorized script.

sections.title: My First Kreyòl Conversation
sections.description: Map the conversation, rehearse useful scenes, then complete a sustained beginner exchange.

topics.title: Build Your Conversation Map
topics.summary: Connect greetings, identity, everyday information, actions, questions, quantities, and time.
learningGoals: Recognize useful openings and transitions inside a conversation.
Choose a question based on information that is still missing.
Reuse familiar identity, action, quantity, and time language without adding new grammar.

topics.title: Rehearse Real Conversation Turns
topics.summary: Practice short scenes about things, actions, quantities, questions, and time.
learningGoals: Respond to short Jan-and-Mari exchanges without relying on English word order.
Reuse ownership and current-action language inside conversation.
Use quantity and schedule language inside practical exchanges.

topics.title: My First Kreyòl Conversation
topics.summary: Complete and understand a sustained beginner conversation using Course 1 language.
learningGoals: Follow a sustained Jan-and-Mari conversation from greeting through closing.
Choose and produce familiar responses based on conversational meaning.
Understand a second version without requiring the exact same order or wording.
